data._comment_features: FIRST-YEAR features only, enforced in nlst_dataset.py. Default exclusions drop the two identifiers; the label reaches the model through the expansion-flag embedding instead of the clinical vector. For literal NAMD parity set excluded_features to [] and clinical_dim to 16 (matches ehr_encoder.EHREncoder in_dim=16).

_comment_budget: One epoch is one pass of the balanced sampler = 2 * 725 majority samples = 91 steps at batch 16. `epochs` overrides `steps`. val/loss is evaluated every epoch (cheap, deterministic) and the best checkpoint is written to model-best.pt; the expensive sampling-based image metrics run on sample_metrics_every.
_comment_noflag: NO ORACLE FLAG. HemExp's expansion-flag input maps to the NLST malignancy label, so conditioning on it leaks the label into the generated image: the flagged run scored ROC-AUC 0.9009 against a 0.8136 real-image ceiling, which is impossible for a faithful generator. The arms this is compared against (ctclip, pred_clip, alignvae) condition on a prompt built from feature indices 0..14 and never see the label at index 15. Setting use_expansion_flag_input=false removes the flag embedding entirely (verified: output is bit-identical for flag=0 vs flag=1). Clinical conditioning is unchanged: 13 dims of first-year biomarkers + EHR, with label already excluded.
_comment_parity: STRICT PARITY WITH THE NAMD ARMS. Three differences from the first arm, all of which favoured HemExp: (1) 64x64 centre crop, not the full 128x128 field -- the benchmark arms see only the crop, so conditioning on 4x the context was not a fair comparison; (2) no oracle expansion flag -- it maps to the malignancy label and leaked it into the pixels (ROC-AUC 0.9009 vs a 0.8136 real-image ceiling); (3) no label-balanced batches -- the NAMD arms train on the natural ~19% positive rate, HemExp was training on 50/50.
